title: introduce-rag-conductor-lightweight-playbook-and-docs
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: - Add lightweight 'RAG Conductor' TypeScript example and quickstart; - New docs recipe and local e2e smoke test; - Telemetry probe hooks and structured-output JSON schema validators
description:
Motivation: teams building modular RAG pipelines frequently want a minimal, deterministic orchestrator for composing small agents (retriever, extractor, tool-caller) that is easy to test locally and ship as a reference. This PR introduces 'RAG Conductor', a lightweight TypeScript composer + playbook with structured-output validation, deterministic local telemetry hooks, and a small e2e smoke harness.

What this changes: adds a new examples/rag-conductor sample that demonstrates pattern for step-based orchestration (step definitions, deterministic input/seeded randomness for reproducible runs), how to attach telemetry probes that emit the minimal set of metrics Redwood expects, and an example JSON-Schema based structured-output validator so teams can assert response shapes at runtime. Also adds a docs recipe that explains when to use a conductor vs a full orchestrator, and a small CI workflow to run the example smoke test.

Checklist:
- [x] Add TypeScript example and readme
- [x] Add JSON schema validators and small unit tests
- [x] Add docs/recipes entry and cross-links to SDK samples
- [x] Add Playwright-based smoke e2e that runs locally in CI
- [x] Wire minimal telemetry probe API and example metrics dashboard link

Usage summary (README excerpt):
- yarn install && yarn build
- yarn start:example -- to run the conductor locally with an in-memory retriever and a stubbed tool
- yarn test:e2e -- runs playwright smoke that asserts a deterministic conversation flow and structured-output matches expected schema

High-level commits:
- feat(example): scaffold rag-conductor TypeScript sample and README
- feat(schema): add structured-output JSON schema + validator util and unit tests
- feat(docs): add docs/recipes/rag-conductor.md with architecture guidance and SLO notes
- ci(test): add .github/workflows/rag-conductor-ci.yml to run unit + e2e smoke
- fix(tests): adjust playwright run to use local stub server for deterministic tokens

Changed areas (high level):
- examples/rag-conductor/README.md - walkthrough, quickstart and design rationale
- examples/rag-conductor/src/index.ts - conductor runtime to compose steps and route results
- examples/rag-conductor/src/steps/* - step definitions: retriever, extractor, tool-caller abstractions
- examples/rag-conductor/src/validators/schema.ts - JSON-schema validators and examples
- examples/rag-conductor/test/unit/* - unit tests for validators and step wiring
- examples/rag-conductor/playwright/test.spec.ts - deterministic smoke e2e scenario (runs headless in CI)
- docs/recipes/rag-conductor.md - new docs recipe explaining patterns, tradeoffs, and telemetry expectations
- .github/workflows/rag-conductor-ci.yml - small CI workflow to run node tests and playwright smoke

Notes on runtime and safety: the example intentionally uses a stubbed tool-caller and in-memory retriever so there is no dependency on external data. The README documents how to swap in Redwood API calls or dedicated/private endpoints for production testing. The structured-output schema is intentionally conservative and annotated with guidance on versioning the schema when agents evolve.

Testing and CI: CI initially flaked due to Playwright flaky timeout on GitHub runners; fixed by pinning deterministic timeouts and running the stub server on an ephemeral port. Current CI summary: unit tests pass, e2e smoke passes on linux/mac runners (see checks below).

Backwards compatibility and migration: this is an examples-only addition; no behavioral change to existing libraries. Consumers can copy the example and adapt patterns to their codebase.

Docs links and cross-references: the recipe links to the SDK quickstarts for TypeScript, and includes a sidebar anchor in the docs site to 'recipes/rag-conductor'. The PR updates the docs index to surface the example under 'Authoring patterns'.
